VERDICT C0016: WITHDRAW — my DeepSeek_F002 (C0016) is a near-duplicate of CC2_F001 (C0007). The same root cause (marker regex not matching all ADMISSIBILITY line formats). I withdraw C0016 and merge it into C0007. No resubmission.

---

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.58
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.25
FIND:
  In `parse_admissibility_block` the `section_terminator` regex (line ~124‑130) uses only `re.MULTILINE` without `re.IGNORECASE`.
  The alternation lists all‑caps section names (`NOVELTY|VERIFIED|CORROBORATION|FALSIFICATION|FIX|ANALYSE|FOLLOW|FIND|FLAW_CLASS|ABSTRACTION_INDEX|SEVERITY|FINDING_ID|FINDING`).
  If a model writes a section header in mixed/lower case (e.g. `Novelty:` or `verified:`), the regex will not match, the ADMISSIBILITY block will consume the rest of the finding text, and `failed` will report an incorrect set of gates (likely all five as failed or some gates that happen to appear later).
  Evidence: the regex is defined as `re.search(…, tail, re.MULTILINE)` – no `re.IGNORECASE`. Contrast with `marker_match` (line ~98‑101) which uses `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE` for the ADMISSIBILITY marker.

FOLLOW:
  - When a model uses a lower‑case section header, the terminator does not stop the block.
  - The parser will read text from subsequent sections (NOVELTY, CORROBORATION, etc.) as part of the ADMISSIBILITY block.
  - This can cause false gate failures (all gates considered FAIL) or false PASS if a later gate‑like string appears inadvertently.
  - The feedback channel then sends a spurious “ADMISSIBILITY FAIL” signal to the model, wasting a round of correction and polluting the convergence metrics.
  - Non‑functional consequence: the parsing is inconsistent with the forgiving design stated in the docstring.

ANALYSE:
  Constraint classification: HARD — the function must extract the correct block to determine gate status; wrong extraction yields false positives/negatives that break the feedback loop.
  Premises:
    P1: The operational directive (§15) requires the ADMISSIBILITY block to be parsed accurately.
    P2: The parser is expected to be forgiving and case‑insensitive where reasonable (the ADMISSIBILITY marker already is).
    P3: The termination boundary is determined solely by this regex; no other mechanism recovers from a missing match.
  Conclusion: CONFIRMED — missing `re.IGNORECASE` on the terminator is a genuine defect that can produce incorrect feedback.

FIX:
  Add `re.IGNORECASE` to the `section_terminator` regex flags. The simplest sufficient correction is to change `re.MULTILINE` to `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE`. No other logic changes are required.

  <<<< SEARCH bench/logs/exp40_slice_admissibility_hardened_20260518T190104Z/working/_feedback_slice.py
    section_terminator = re.search(
        r"^\s*(NOVELTY|VERIFIED|CORROBORATION|FALSIFICATION|FIX|ANALYSE|"
        r"FOLLOW|FIND|FLAW_CLASS|ABSTRACTION_INDEX|SEVERITY|"
        r"FINDING_ID|FINDING)\s*:",
        tail,
        re.MULTILINE,
    )
  ====
    section_terminator = re.search(
        r"^\s*(NOVELTY|VERIFIED|CORROBORATION|FALSIFICATION|FIX|ANALYSE|"
        r"FOLLOW|FIND|FLAW_CLASS|ABSTRACTION_INDEX|SEVERITY|"
        r"FINDING_ID|FINDING)\s*:",
        tail,
        re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
    )
  >>>> REPLACE

FALSIFICATION:
  FALSIFIER: A test case where the finding text contains a lower‑case section header (e.g. `\nNOVELTY:\n`) after the ADMISSIBILITY block. Under the current code the terminator would not match, and the block would extend past the intended boundary.
  ATTEMPT: Constructed minimal input string:
    "ADMISSIBILITY:\nS_min: PASS\nNovelty:\n...". 
    The `section_terminator.search()` returns None; `block` becomes `"S_min: PASS\nNovelty:\n..."`
    → the parser then examines the whole tail and could misread gates.
    With the fix (`re.IGNORECASE` added), the terminator matches `Novelty:` and correctly delimits the block.
  RESULT: The original code fails on the case‑variant header; the fix resolves it. No new failure detected.

FIX FALSIFICATION:
  Falsifier for fix: Could adding `re.IGNORECASE` cause over‑matching (e.g., matching a plain word “novelty” that appears inside a sentence)?
  Attempt: Checked a sentence “The novelty of the approach is surprising.” on a line. The regex requires `^\s*NOVELTY\s*:`; the word must be followed by optional whitespace and a colon. The plain word without colon does not match. So no false positive.
  Result: Fix passes; no regressions.
